invariants: theta_k is the kth-largest certified lower endpoint across every eligible item.
Retain every item with upper >= theta_k; exclude only upper < theta_k.
At least k exact scores are >= theta_k because at least k lower endpoints are >= theta_k.
An excluded item's exact score is strictly below theta_k and therefore cannot enter exact top-k.
Exact reranking the retained set under the canonical score and stable-ID order returns the full-scan top-k.
This proof is valid only if all eligible records are covered by valid conservative intervals.
A candidate index that omits records without an admissible aggregate bound cannot produce ExactComplete.
Real-arithmetic interval formulas are not sufficient until outward rounding encloses the canonical f32 score.
